tips.text: Run `npm run doctor` whenever something seems off. It checks every hub component and says how to fix what it finds.
Run `npm run self-check -- builder` for a short readiness report on one agent: its profile, skills and memory.
Run `npm run version:check` to see whether a newer hub release is available.
Run `npm run list` to see every project's todo, in-flight and done tasks in one view.
Run `npm run install-skill -- <name>` to add an optional skill to your hub, for example `frontend-design`.
Run `npm.cmd run check:tickets -- --hub-root .` to catch task files whose state no longer matches their GitHub issue.
Run `npm run memory-index:build`, then search your agents' memory by keyword with `npm run memory-index -- find <keyword>`.

You don't need to remember skill names. Open any skill's SKILL.md in your provider's skills folder. Its description line has a "Use when:" list of trigger phrases. Say one of those phrases to your agent and the skill loads.
Tell your agent "grill me", "let's brainstorm", or "walk me through" a decision and it starts a one-question-at-a-time design interrogation.
Tell Architect "audit assumptions", "check for hidden assumptions", or "what am I assuming" on a ticket before it goes to Builder, and it runs a hidden-assumptions audit pass.
Tell Architect "did we miss anything from my old hub" or "check what didn't get migrated" and it runs a completeness pass against your prior migration.
Tell Architect "how hard" it would be to rewrite this codebase, or ask for a "security audit", and it runs a structured security-and-feasibility pass.
Tell Architect you "inherited" this codebase, or that it's an "unfamiliar codebase", before a refactor, and it typically starts an investigation pass.
Tell your agent to find the "root cause" when "tests fail" or you hit an "unexpected error", and it runs a systematic debugging pass instead of guessing.
Tell your agent to review this PR "before merging" it, or ask for a "code review", and it runs a multi-axis quality pass across the diff.
Tell Architect "Good morning Team" or ask for a "start-of-day briefing" and it runs the whole team's morning briefing for you.
Tell Architect "Good night Team", "Wrapping up", or "EOD" at day's end and it consolidates and archives the session.

To switch projects, start a fresh session (or clear the current one), greet your agent ("Hi Architect"), then tell it which project to work on, for example "Let's work on project <name>". A clean start keeps the old project's context from leaking into the new one.
